research_validity_registry.result_summary: Walk-forward over 7 monthly folds on the 7 standard BET leagues, identical training rows and identical test fixtures, differing only in the 13 restored corners/HT features: log loss 0.69251 (OLD, 52 features) vs 0.69196 (NEW, 65). NEW won 5 of 7 months by 0.0005-0.002. AUC 0.5119 vs 0.5174.
research_validity_registry.significance: The retrain reported AUC 0.534 -> 0.709, but that was measured across two DIFFERENT test sets (n_test 3,570 -> 5,558) and over the whole training universe, not the bet leagues. On bet leagues the model barely discriminates.
research_validity_registry.KNOWN_LIMITATION: The experiment's models have a prediction spread of 0.026 against production's 0.207, because it trains only on the 22,869 standard bet-league rows while production trains on the full universe. Its P&L therefore does NOT describe the deployed model and must not be quoted as such.
research_validity_registry.status_of_conclusion: Restored features add nothing measurable: SUPPORTED. Deployed model better or worse in money terms: UNKNOWN.

research_validity_registry.NOT: BETTING_EDGE. Recovering canonical player history measurably improves PREDICTION. It does not create, and is not evidence of, a betting edge, and it does not change real_money_enabled for props.

research_validity_registry.result_summary: A large increase in training fixtures produced only a small, inconsistent predictive gain. The restored corners/HT feature families were worth 0.0005-0.002 log loss across 7 monthly folds on the 7 standard BET leagues, against the 0.048 the retrain metrics appeared to claim.
research_validity_registry.caution: MORE ROWS != BETTER MODEL. The retrain's AUC 0.534 -> 0.709 was measured across two DIFFERENT test sets (n_test 3,570 -> 5,558) and over the whole training universe, not the bet leagues. On bet leagues AUC was 0.512-0.517.

research_validity_registry.question: Does repeatedly retraining on accumulated football experience improve FUTURE prediction versus a frozen model?
research_validity_registry.current_answer: Yes on player prediction quality: frozen is the worst of the three variants on all three metrics (LL 0.25525 / AUC 0.73591 / PR-AUC 0.21295) and canonical the best. This is SEPARATE from architecture and separate from betting edge.

product_boundary.architecture: V9 / approved Pro outputs -> WOWZA PRODUCT PUBLISHER -> Product Database -> Wowza API -> Web / Android / future clients
product_boundary.immutable_history_invariant: A changed probability is published as a NEW snapshot. 14:00, 16:00 and 18:00 are three snapshots, never one overwritten value. Neither a retrain nor a pre-match update may rewrite history.
product_boundary.frontend_rule: The UI must NEVER decide FORECAST/PAPER/VALIDATED/LIVE. That state arrives from the backend publication contract; the UI only renders it.
product_boundary.claim_safety: Never convert 'AUC improved' into 'profitable betting system'. Never convert 'player scorer model predicts better' into 'player scorer bets have edge'. Prediction quality, calibration, market residual, CLV, historical betting ROI and prospective betting ROI are six different things.

known_ambiguities.item: player_history.parquet size vs GitHub's 100 MB limit
known_ambiguities.why: On 2026-09-24 the file went 316,157 -> 501,474 rows and 135 MB, and `git push` was REJECTED with GH001. A float32/int32 downcast plus zstd brought it to 90.6 MB (verified: same rows, same columns, ids byte-identical, worst relative float error 5.96e-08) and it pushed. That is a STOPGAP with ~9 MB of headroom on a file that grew 48 MB in one afternoon. Seasons 2023-2024 are still uncollected and would breach the limit again. Git LFS, splitting the file, or not committing it at all is an architecture decision that must be made BEFORE the next depth increase. The backfill is deliberately paused pending it.
